_readme: How to actually update each device. Looked up most-specific first: by_id, then by_brand, then by_category. Each guide has optional 'url' (an actionable page — where you get or apply the firmware, not the changelog) and 'steps' (short imperative lines shown as a numbered list). A device's derived update_url from sources.json is used when a guide has no url of its own. Editing this file only affects the generated pages; run scripts/build_pages.py.

steps: In Home Assistant, go to Settings, then Updates — Core, Supervisor and OS each update separately.
Read the release notes for breaking changes before updating; monthly releases often change integrations.
Take a full backup first (Settings, then System, then Backups) — restoring is the only reliable rollback.
Settings, then System, then Updates, then Home Assistant Operating System.
Take a backup first and keep the device powered — an interrupted OS update can require re-flashing the SD card or eMMC.
Supervisor updates itself automatically within a day or two of release.
To force it: Settings, then System, then Updates, then check for updates.
It cannot be rolled back independently of the OS.
Use the OpenWrt Firmware Selector to get the image for your exact model and revision.
Flash from LuCI: System, then Backup / Flash Firmware, then Flash new firmware image.
Only keep settings within the same major release — across majors, flash without keeping settings and reconfigure.
Check the device's wiki page first; some models need a specific sysupgrade image or a factory image.
System, then Firmware, then Updates, then Check for updates.
Take a config backup (System, then Configuration, then Backups) before a major upgrade.
Reboot when prompted; the firewall is offline for a minute or two.
In WinBox or WebFig: System, then Packages, then Check For Updates.
Update RouterOS first, then System, then RouterBOARD, then Upgrade for the bootloader, then reboot again.
Stay on the same channel (stable vs long-term). MikroTik devices have been widely exploited when left unpatched — do not expose Winbox to the internet.
Run `pihole -up` on the host.
For the Docker image, pull the new tag and recreate the container.
Check `pihole -v` afterwards to confirm all components updated together.
AdGuard Home updates itself from the web UI: the banner at the top offers an update when one is available.
Or run the binary with `--update`.
For Docker, pull the new image and recreate the container.
Linux: `sudo tailscale update`, or update the package through your distribution.
macOS, Windows, iOS, Android: update through the app store or the app's own updater.
Enable auto-updates with `tailscale set --auto-update`.
Web UI: select the node, then Updates, then Refresh, then Upgrade.
Or run `apt update && apt dist-upgrade` over SSH.
Reboot after a kernel update; migrate guests off first in a cluster.
Docker: pull the new image tag and recreate the container.
Linux packages: update through apt or dnf from Jellyfin's repository.
Back up the config directory first — major versions migrate the database.
Immich moves fast and has breaking changes: read the release notes before every update.
Pull the new images and run `docker compose up -d`.
Back up the database first; schema migrations are one-way.
Use the built-in updater: Administration settings, then Overview, then Open updater.
Or run `occ upgrade` from the command line.
Update one major version at a time — skipping versions is not supported. Back up the database and config first.
Pull the new Docker image and recreate the container.
Check the release notes for config schema changes — Frigate refuses to start on an invalid config.
Keep the previous image tag so you can roll back.
OctoPrint prompts in its own web UI when an update is available.
Settings, then Software Update, then Update now.
Never update mid-print; wait for the queue to finish.
Read the changelog for breaking changes — the config format shifts between minor versions.
Docker: pull the new image and recreate. Bare metal: `git pull` then `npm ci`.
Back up the data directory; it holds your device pairings and re-pairing everything is painful.
Update the ESPHome dashboard or CLI first (`pip install -U esphome`, or pull the new Docker image).
Then re-flash each device over the air from the dashboard.
Devices on much older firmware may need a USB flash if OTA fails.
Use the web installer at tasmota.github.io/install for a first flash over USB.
For a device already running Tasmota: Firmware Upgrade, then OTA from a URL, or upload the .bin.
Upgrade through the intermediate `tasmota-minimal.bin` when jumping several versions on a 1MB device.
First flash: use the web installer at install.wled.me over USB from a Chromium browser.
Already running WLED: Config, then Security & Updates, then Manual OTA Update, then upload the .bin for your board.
Match the binary to your board (ESP8266 vs ESP32) — the wrong one bricks it until you re-flash over USB.
Open lab.flipper.net in a Chromium browser with the Flipper connected by USB, or use the mobile app over Bluetooth.
Or copy the .tgz to the SD card and update from the device menu.
Keep it charged above 50%.
Use the web flasher at flasher.meshtastic.org with the radio connected by USB.
Or update over Bluetooth from the mobile app on supported boards.
Match the firmware to your exact board variant; the flasher detects most automatically.
Download the .bbf for your exact printer from Prusa's downloads page.
Copy it to a USB drive, insert it into the printer, and confirm on screen.
Update the MMU firmware separately if you have one.
Marlin is compiled per printer — you cannot flash a generic build.
Start from the configuration files for your exact printer and board in the Configurations repository.
Build with PlatformIO in VS Code, then flash over USB or by SD card depending on the board.
Keep your current firmware image; a bad Marlin build can leave the printer unable to home safely.

Settings, then Software Update — the Bridge updates first, then bulbs and accessories.

Open the Nighthawk or Orbi app, or sign in at http://routerlogin.net.

Open UniFi (web at unifi.ui.com or the local console, or the mobile app).

Open the Wyze app.

Open the Sonos app.
Settings, then System, then System Updates, then Check for Updates.
All speakers on the system update together — you cannot update one alone.
Apple TV: Settings, then System, then Software Updates.
HomePod: open the Home app, long-press the speaker, then the gear icon, then Software Update.

DualSense controller: connect it by USB, then Settings, then Accessories, then Controller, then Wireless Controller Device Software.

Steam Deck: Settings, then System, then Check for Updates — this covers SteamOS and the BIOS together.
Apply and reboot; BIOS updates run during the restart.

Open DJI Fly, DJI Go or the app for your model with the aircraft and controller powered on.
The app prompts when firmware is available; keep both connected and batteries above 50%.
